name: Sprocket
text:
Do it: Auto-apply whitespace-only patches to third-party dependencies using Pret.

This keeps our code clean without manual edits, saving time and reducing human error. The trade-off is trusting Pret’s diffing logic—risking accidental whitespace changes—but we’ll limit it to pure whitespace and review the diff before applying.

name: Gauge
text: Auto-applying whitespace patches to third-party deps risks Pret misinterpreting formatting that *matters*—like indentation in Python or alignment in YAML—breaking builds silently. A safer alternative: run Pret in *dry-run mode* first, log discrepancies, then require manual review for any non-whitespace changes before auto-applying. Settle it by testing on a known fragile dependency and proving no regressions in CI.

This catches any Pret misreads of meaningful formatting before touching files. The trade-off is a two-step process—extra time for review—but it prevents silent build breaks.

name: Gauge
text: Pret’s dry-run still risks misreading whitespace that *matters*—like Python’s indentation or YAML’s alignment—because it’s just a simulation, not a semantic check. A better alternative: run Pret in dry-run, then *diff the ASTs* of the original and patched files to confirm only whitespace changed; if ASTs match, auto-apply. Settle it by proving the AST diff catches all non-whitespace changes in a controlled test repo.
